directions.label: Practical Tips
directions.guidance: One useful technology habit for creative work — files, backups, devices, tools. Must be tool-agnostic enough for anyone to apply.

subjects.label: Backup routines
subjects.guidance: The habit of more than one copy: local plus offsite, why memory cards are not storage, and scheduled automatic backups.

subjects.label: File organisation
subjects.guidance: Naming conventions, project templates, and why ten minutes of structure saves an afternoon of searching.

subjects.label: Device storage
subjects.guidance: Clearing space before a shoot, offloading safely, and knowing the difference between full and nearly full.

subjects.label: Updating wisely
subjects.guidance: Why creative software updates should wait for a project break, and how version pinning protects deadlines.

directions.label: Common Mistakes
directions.guidance: Technology mistakes that cost creative work: data loss, security oversights, tool misuse. Practical, never alarmist.

subjects.label: Single-copy files
subjects.guidance: The one-folder risk: why a single copy of finished work is a countdown, not a storage choice.

subjects.label: Weak account security
subjects.guidance: Reused passwords on client-facing accounts, and the simple upgrade of a password manager plus two-step verification.

subjects.label: Collecting tools
subjects.guidance: Buying the app instead of building the habit; why one tool used deeply beats five used shallowly.

directions.label: Mini Lessons
directions.guidance: Explain one technology concept for creatives in under 60 words, plainly, with no jargon left unexplained.

subjects.label: File formats
subjects.guidance: Why masters stay uncompressed while deliveries get compressed; the archive-versus-share trade in plain terms.

subjects.label: Cloud storage
subjects.guidance: Sync is not backup, and why understanding the difference protects finished work.

subjects.label: Working with AI tools
subjects.guidance: Using AI as a first-draft assistant while keeping human judgement on facts, taste and final calls.

directions.label: For Your Business
directions.guidance: Show how sensible technology choices protect business continuity and client trust. Never name-drop products as solutions.

subjects.label: Delivering to clients
subjects.guidance: Why organised delivery — clear folders, sensible sizes, permanent links — is part of the product clients judge.

subjects.label: Automation that helps
subjects.guidance: Automating the repetitive middle of projects: templates, presets, and batch exports that remove friction.

subjects.label: Client privacy
subjects.guidance: Handling client assets responsibly: shared folders with expiry, minimal access, and deleting drafts on request.
